title: {{NAME}} and the Invincible League
moral: Power is most honourable when it chooses restraint.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a royal gold and black soccer hero jersey, black shorts, and gold-black cleats — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
The Hero Football League had a problem.

The heroes in it had powers.

This sounds like an advantage. It was also, as {{NAME}} had been pointing out for two seasons, making the game less interesting.

A striker with super-speed could outrun any defence. A goalkeeper with force fields could stop any shot. A midfielder who could freeze time had recently scored seventeen goals in one match before the referee retired on the spot.

Princess Mira, the league commissioner, called an emergency session.

She asked {{NAME}} to present the solution.

pages.content:
{{NAME}}'s proposal: voluntary power limitation by category.

Speed limited to twice human maximum. Force fields during set plays only. Temporal abilities: banned entirely. Strength: applied to movement, not to hitting the ball.

"The point is the football," he said. "Not the powers. The powers are supposed to make you good at football. They don't do that if they bypass it."

Princess Mira looked around the table.

"Objections?"

The hero who had scored seventeen goals raised a hand.

"Anyone's objection other than him," she said.

pages.content:
The new-format season started three weeks later.

With limitations in place, the football was genuinely competitive: speed of twice-human was still superhuman, still spectacular, but it could be tracked and defended against.

{{NAME}}'s own team: he had no powers. He had always played on skill and tactical intelligence alone.

In the new format, that was no longer a disadvantage.

In the first match of the new season, he scored twice. Against a team with three super-speed players.

The crowd made a noise he had never heard before at his goals.

pages.content:
The hero who had scored seventeen games found, by week four, that he was enjoying the new format.

"It's harder," he told {{NAME}} after a match.

"Yes."

"It feels better when I score."

"Yes."

"I scored three times last week," he said. "It felt like three times more than seventeen did before."

{{NAME}} understood completely.

"That's what challenge is for," he said.

pages.content:
The season ended with the most watched final in the league's history.

Princess Mira presented the trophy in the stadium.

{{NAME}}'s team had finished third.

But he had scored nine goals, which was the most he had ever scored, and every one had been a real goal.

In bed that night, he replayed all nine.

The ninth was the best.

He fell asleep in the middle of replaying it and his dream picked up exactly where he left off, and the ball went in, and it was exactly as good as it had been.
